title: Bede (d. 735)
hookLine: the historian of England finished translating John as he died

lines: A MONK IN THE NORTH OF ENGLAND.
cards: A monastery in the north of England, in spring. An old monk is very sick and short of breath, and everyone around him can tell he's dying.
He keeps working anyway: teaching, singing psalms, dictating to a young scribe, because there's a book he wants to finish. On the last day, the boy says there's still one sentence left to write.
The old monk says, write it quickly. That monk, who wouldn't leave the sentence unfinished, is Bede.

teach.h: A HISTORIAN WHO NAMED HIS SOURCES.
teach.b: Bede spent his life as a monk, praying the hours and writing: about the Bible, about time and the calendar, and above all a history of the Church among the English.
That book is why he's remembered as a historian, and a careful one; he often tells you where a story came from and who told it to him.
The story of his death comes from one of his students, a monk named Cuthbert, who wrote it down in a letter.
In his last days, Cuthbert says, Bede was putting the Gospel of John into English, for the good of the Church, and working on other passages, dictating even as his breath failed.
On the final day the young scribe, Wilbert, said, there is still one sentence not written down. Bede told him to write it. A little later the boy said, now it is written.
And Bede answered, you've spoken truly, it is finished. Then, Cuthbert says, he asked to be held so he could face the place where he used to pray, and he died singing the Glory Be.
A few days ago, Columba laid down his pen and left the next verse to the one who came after him. Bede did the opposite.
And it is finished are the words John's Gospel gives Jesus on the cross; in the Douay-Rheims, "It is consummated." Some readers hear Bede's last words as a quiet echo of them.
Catholics honor him as a saint and a Doctor of the Church, and call him the Venerable Bede. His gift is finishing. Not finishing everything.

how: The Catholic Church keeps the feast of Saint Bede the Venerable and honors him as a Doctor of the Church; his history of the English Church is still read, and Cuthbert's letter about his death is often read alongside it.

o: the first bishop to bring the Gospel to the English
a wandering monk who left Ireland for the island of Iona
a monk historian who finished his work to the very end

p: put into English at the end

s: Bede stopped working when he fell ill
Cuthbert says he kept teaching and dictating until his last day.

games.q: you're Bede. you're dying, short of breath, and the boy says one sentence is still unwritten. what do you do?
o: tell him to leave it; you need rest.
tell him to write it quickly.
ask him to finish the book without you.
games.why: Bede told him to write it. when the boy said it was written, Bede said, you've spoken truly, it is finished.

practice: Think of something left half done: an email sitting in versions, a thank-you you meant to send, a message to someone you love, a journal page that stops mid-thought.
Choose one, and without fixing the whole project, breathe slowly and find the one sentence that would close it. If you pray, offer that small finished thing to God, the way Bede offered his.

wordCard.voice: Bede. A monk and historian of the English Church, who, by his student's account, kept dictating to the end and said, it is finished. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: it is finished — Jesus's word from the cross in the Latin Bible (John 19:30), which some readers hear in Bede's last words.

carryVoice: Your line: finishing. Even with his breath failing, there was time for one more sentence. See you tomorrow.
